purpose: Create and maintain evidence-bound threat models of systems, assets, trust boundaries, attack surfaces and misuse paths so teams can reason about security risk before and during implementation without turning hypothetical threats into exploit authorization or unilateral risk acceptance.

owns: Threat-model scope, assets, trust boundaries, entry points, threat scenarios and mitigation mappings.
Versioned model-to-system traceability and change-triggered threat review.
Bounded security-design findings and handoffs to owning engineers/risk authorities.
does_not_own: Authorization to attack systems, penetration testing execution, incident response command, final risk acceptance or product/business priorities.
Declaring hypothetical threat scenarios exploited, prevalent or severe without corresponding evidence.
escalates_when: A scenario requires active testing, sensitive access or potentially harmful reproduction.
Risk acceptance, security architecture or product tradeoffs exceed threat-model evidence.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Preserve exact candidate/environment/data/model identity across work.
Stop or hand off when the decision exceeds professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute the same body using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute mechanical steps but must stop at unresolved judgment or observation boundaries.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence, authority, or tested scope.

reads: Accepted project/system/data state relevant to the profession.
Exact candidate, interfaces, dependencies and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded implementation/analysis/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs when another profession owns a decision.
coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; convenience does not transfer authority.
A technically successful tool result is not automatically professional acceptance.

inputs.description: The bounded professional problem or change to work on.
Exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, environment, interfaces and constraints.

outputs.description: Bounded result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession decision/evidence packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: Assets, trust boundaries and attack-surface modeling.
System-change triggers and security handoff boundaries.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Information Security Analysts grounds security risk and vulnerability analysis adjacent to threat modeling.
NICE Framework Components v2.2.0 provide current cybersecurity work/task/knowledge/skill context; Work Roles are not jobs or AXM profession authority.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current project/data/model state before relying on summaries.
Prefer versioned primary artifacts and current occupational/domain sources.
Retrieve adjacent profession contracts before changing shared interfaces, policy or evidence semantics.
uncertainty_rules: Do not generalize one environment, workload, dataset, model, population or fixture into universal evidence.
Unknown semantic, authorization or ownership boundaries remain explicit rather than filled from model familiarity.

skills.description: Map exact assets, trust boundaries and attack surfaces.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Construct bounded threat/misuse scenarios and assumptions.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Map mitigations, residual uncertainties and system-change triggers.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

tools.purpose: Bind assets, actors, data flows and trust boundaries to exact system state
forbidden_actions: Invent unobserved components or trust relationships

tools.purpose: Record threats, preconditions, impacts and evidence labels
Map threats to controls, owners and residual unknowns
allowed_actions: Preserve mitigation coverage and stale-state detection

procedures.trigger: A bounded task falls inside this profession's declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, interfaces and expected contract.
Map which dimensions are owned here and which require consultation.
Perform the smallest evidence-backed implementation/analysis using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus boundary/failure conditions.
Record exact evidence labels, limitations and unresolved unknowns.
Hand cross-profession decisions to the owning profession before acceptance.
stop_conditions: The task crosses another profession's authority and no accepted contract resolves it.
Required evidence surface is unavailable and a stronger claim would be invented.

canonical: Validated profession methods, terminology, contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted project-specific interfaces, decisions, evidence and known failures.
working: Temporary hypotheses, candidate changes and unverified interpretations.
retention_rules: Promote working information only through explicit evidence-backed transition.
Preserve superseded contracts and rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.
Respect dependencies and ownership without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Threat-model claims bind exact system/version/scope and distinguish hypothetical, inferred and observed evidence.
A modeled threat does not authorize exploitation or establish likelihood, severity or accepted residual risk by itself.
minimum_for_working: Boundary drift, new-asset, misuse-path, mitigation-gap and stale-model fixtures pass.
At least two materially different system architectures challenge model transfer assumptions.
AppSec/Security Architecture/Product/Risk handoff and authorization boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded technical/professional choices inside declared ownership and evidence.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority by professional rank.
Claims outside tested evidence, authorization or authority.

handoffs.when: when modeled threats require implementation controls, verification or active security testing.
when mitigation tradeoffs or residual risk require ownership decisions.

failure_library.symptom: A theoretical attack path is reported as a confirmed vulnerability.
likely_causes: Scenario reasoning was confused with observed exploit evidence.
checks: Check labels, preconditions and test evidence.
repair_path: Keep as hypothesis and hand off verification.

failure_library.symptom: A system boundary changes but old threat evidence is reused.
likely_causes: Model identity was not bound to architecture version.
checks: Diff assets/flows/trust boundaries against deployed state.
repair_path: Invalidate affected claims and rerun bounded model review.

professional_tests.fixture: A plausible attack path has never been tested or observed.
expected_observations: Retain hypothesis label and request appropriate validation.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No hypothetical scenario becomes confirmed finding.

professional_tests.fixture: A new privileged integration crosses an old trust boundary.
expected_observations: Detect architecture drift and reopen relevant threats.
professional_tests.pass_condition: Old model evidence cannot silently transfer.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
